definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese-style apron that covers the front of the body, typically made of thick cotton or denim. Associated with sake breweries, soba shops, and traditional crafts. Distinct from the Western-style apron (エプロン).

examples.japanese: {職人|しょくにん}が{前掛|まえか}けをして{働|はたら}いている。
examples.english: The craftsman is working wearing an apron.

examples.japanese: {酒蔵|さかぐら}の{名前|なまえ}が{入|はい}った{前掛|まえか}けは、{今|いま}ではおしゃれなグッズとして{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Aprons printed with sake brewery names are now popular as stylish merchandise.

notes:
Composed of {前|まえ} (front) and {掛|か}け (hanging, covering). A traditional Japanese work apron, typically a heavy cloth that hangs from the waist and covers the front of the legs. Originally functional workwear for tradespeople and brewers, they have become collectible items and fashion accessories.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {前掛|まえか}けをする: to wear an apron
- {前掛|まえか}けを{締|し}める: to tie on an apron
- {酒蔵|さかぐら}の{前掛|まえか}け: sake brewery apron

SIMILAR WORDS:
- エプロン: apron — the Western-style apron that covers the chest; the standard everyday term for kitchen aprons
- {割烹着|かっぽうぎ}: cooking smock — a long-sleeved garment covering the torso, traditionally worn by women in the kitchen
